OUTAGE REGIMES · NOS · SEP 2024–AUG 2026

What happens to limits and flow when a specific network outage is in place

This section adds a network-outage dimension to the regime report. AEMO Network Outage Schedule (NOS) bookings are linked to the constraint-set families they invoke and to the actual invocation record. The equations in those families are checked against the reconstructed envelope to decide which families are relevant to each connector: a family is relevant only if one of its equations actually set that connector's limit while invoked. Each invoked half-hour is then compared with matched half-hours on the same connector and direction, in the same season, half-hour, day type and weather/VRE/demand regime, within ±21 days, with the family off and, where possible, the same other outage families in place. Treated half-hours are therefore compared with similar conditions rather than with an unconditional average. Outages are scheduled for quiet periods, and a raw average would mostly measure that timing.

The window is two years (two blocks of each Australian season), which is shorter than the three-year flow window above. The analysis is retrospective and descriptive: realised invocations and actual outage times are used, and no forecast feature or fitted model is produced. Limits are dispatch-solution outputs, so an "effect" means a change in the solved envelope, not in physical transfer capability.

Outage episodes37,136NEM-wide bookings overlapping the window (MMSDM final state)
Relevant families410connector × constraint-set pairs that set a limit while invoked
Supported families135pass episodes, hours, match and placebo gates
Lookup assets208outage assets with a supported published level
01

The largest supported reduction

N-ARSR_8E on QNI reverse: -656 MW (-69% of the seasonal median) across 10 episodes and 990 invoked hours.

02

Some outage families raise one direction

I-BURC on VNI forward: +365 MW. Outage sets often re-orient the envelope, tightening one direction while the other is set by a looser equation.

03

Flow only partly follows the limit

Across 69 supported family-directions whose limit falls by more than 25 MW, the median flow change is 36% of the limit change. The rest shows up as lost headroom and more time at the limit.

04

Placebo test is mostly clean, not perfectly

Among families that pass the other gates, the ±7-day placebo is clean for QNI 84%, Directlink 84%, VNI 71%, Heywood 86%, Murraylink 91%, Basslink 100%. Families that fail the placebo are never labelled supported; residual timing confounding remains possible.

05

Location is specific where the data allows

92% of outage assets resolve to a named substation and 68% to coordinates and an area label. Nearby generators are listed electrically (equation sensitivity) and geographically (≤50 km).

06

Many bookings are withdrawn; live ones return early

In year 2, 30% of relevant bookings were withdrawn (median across connectors). Early returns (>1 h, 39%) are far more common than overruns (5%). The 100% booked-to-invoked rate is close to built in, because final-state records link only the sets that were used.

Outage landscape

Share of half-hours in each connector-level state. "Leading" means an invoked relevant family's equation formed the limit. VNI and the South Australian links are almost never outage-free by this definition, so the analysis compares individual families (on vs off) rather than treating "no outage" as the baseline.

Timing and weather

Pooling the matched half-hours of supported families shows when outages matter most in the day, and whether they matter more in hot, high-VRE or high-residual-demand conditions. These are medians of matched differences, split by the condition at the treated half-hour. They are not interaction coefficients.

Flow response and constraint mechanics

The limit and the flow are separate outcomes. Flow also depends on regional prices and offers. When an outage cuts the limit but flow barely changes, the connector simply had spare headroom. When flow falls almost one-for-one, the outage bound dispatch.

The table below shows which equation led the envelope before each supported outage run began, and which led during it. The leader-changed share is the fraction of runs in which the outage replaced the previous leader.

The 25 families with the largest limit changes are shown; all supported families are in nos_leader_transitions.csv.

Spillover to other connectors

A family that is relevant to one connector can still move another connector's limit through shared network paths, even when none of its equations leads there. Rows are the connectors where the family is relevant; columns are connectors where it is not relevant but was measured.

Onset and recovery

Limits are aligned on the start and end of invocation spells and expressed relative to the median at the same half-hour over the previous seven days on which the family was off. Symmetric start and end curves show a clean switch into and out of the outage configuration.

Bookings, unbooked invocations and falsification

Booked-only and withdrawn-booking windows (family not invoked) should show roughly zero effect, and they act as a second falsification check. Unbooked invocations (the family invoked with no live booking within 24 h) are reported separately and are excluded from the family effects above. Most booked-only and withdrawn medians are within ±15 MW, but not all: Heywood withdrawn booking -35 MW; QNI withdrawn booking -38 MW; VNI booked only -20 MW. Other network conditions around booking windows therefore still influence some comparisons, so single-family effects of similar size should be read with caution.

Specific outage lookup

Search by asset (e.g. a line number), substation, area, connector or generator. Each outage asset is published at the most specific level that passes the support gate, in this order: asset × constraint family, then asset, then constraint family, then substation, then area. The published level is shown with each row, so a row published at "K3" describes outages at that substation generally, not that single asset. Electrically near lists DUIDs whose output moves the family's equations (sensitivity −b/a). Within 50 km lists named power stations near the substation (OpenStreetMap). Indicative rows are greyed.

Connector notes

QNI. QNI has 51 relevant outage families; 20 pass the support gate. A relevant family is invoked in 57% of half-hours and leads the limit in 15%. In the forward direction the largest supported reduction is N-TWUL_85 (-570 MW, typically TAMWORTH/BUS/523, central Tamworth). In the reverse direction the largest supported reduction is N-ARSR_8E (-656 MW, typically Armidale-Sapphire 8E 330kV LINE, central Armidale). 19 individual outage assets have supported asset-level entries in the lookup.

Directlink. Directlink has 28 relevant outage families; 16 pass the support gate. A relevant family is invoked in 40% of half-hours and leads the limit in 6%. In the forward direction the largest supported reduction is N-96L_96R_CB4102 (-37 MW, typically TENTFLD/LINE/96R). In the reverse direction the largest supported reduction is Q-LCCP_8859 (-51 MW, typically H58_LARC/LINE/275KV_8859, west of Gladstone (19 km)). 12 individual outage assets have supported asset-level entries in the lookup.

VNI. VNI has 107 relevant outage families; 26 pass the support gate. A relevant family is invoked in 99% of half-hours and leads the limit in 33%. In the forward direction the largest supported reduction is N-DTKV_18_WG_CLOSE (-291 MW, typically DAPTO/LINE/18, central Wollongong). In the reverse direction the largest supported reduction is N-BADP (-130 MW, typically BALRANLD/LINE/X5/1). 27 individual outage assets have supported asset-level entries in the lookup.

Heywood. Heywood has 87 relevant outage families; 28 pass the support gate. A relevant family is invoked in 79% of half-hours and leads the limit in 28%. In the forward direction the largest supported reduction is V-CRML (-197 MW, typically MLTS/LINE/CRTS_MLTS1_500, central Geelong). In the reverse direction the largest supported reduction is S-TBSE (-201 MW, typically S_EAST/LINE/TABSES_1, central Mount Gambier). 32 individual outage assets have supported asset-level entries in the lookup.

Murraylink. Murraylink has 118 relevant outage families; 36 pass the support gate. A relevant family is invoked in 84% of half-hours and leads the limit in 20%. In the forward direction the largest supported reduction is N-BABU (-74 MW, typically BURONGA/LINE/X5/3). In the reverse direction the largest supported reduction is V-HYMO (-55 MW, typically APD/LINE/APD_HYTS2_500). 36 individual outage assets have supported asset-level entries in the lookup.

Basslink. Basslink has 19 relevant outage families; 9 pass the support gate. A relevant family is invoked in 47% of half-hours and leads the limit in 20%. In the forward direction the largest supported reduction is N-TWUL_85 (-44 MW, typically TAMWORTH/BUS/523, central Tamworth). In the reverse direction the largest supported reduction is V-CRML (-41 MW, typically MLTS/LINE/CRTS_MLTS1_500, central Geelong). 9 individual outage assets have supported asset-level entries in the lookup.

Limitations. Outages are scheduled where network operators expect low impact, so these are typical impacts as scheduled. The set-to-connector mapping and relevance filter are retrospective. Year-1 outage records are final-state only. Substation coordinates come from an OpenStreetMap name crosswalk (medium confidence), and unmatched substations are left blank. Matching falls back to coarser cells when exact matches are unavailable; the rung shares and balance diagnostics are in the download. Full definitions are in METHODOLOGY.md and the execution record is execution/nos_outage_regime_v1/.
